deMinimisNotes.UZ: Duty-free allowance for individuals: up to $1,000 (parcel) / $2,000 (air) / $300 (road). 30% single customs payment applies to excess.
deMinimisNotes.US: De Minimis threshold: goods valued up to $800 per person per day enter duty and tax free.
deMinimisNotes.KZ: EAEU allowance: up to €200 (~$220) and 31 kg. 15% duty applies to excess (at least €2 per 1 kg).
deMinimisNotes.RU: EAEU allowance: up to €200 (~$220) and 31 kg. 15% duty applies to excess (at least €2 per 1 kg).
deMinimisNotes.TR: Duty-free parcel threshold: up to €30. Orders exceeding this are subject to 30%–60% tax.
deMinimisNotes.DE: EU regulations: VAT applies from €0 (IOSS). Customs duties apply to orders over €150 (~$165).
deMinimisNotes.AE: Parcels up to 300 AED (~$80) are exempt. Above 300 AED, 5% duty and 5% VAT apply.
deMinimisNotes.CN: Personal parcel limit: 500 CNY (~$70). Cross-border e-commerce tax applies to excess.
deMinimisNotes.KR: Duty-free allowance for personal parcels: up to $150 (from the US — up to $200). 15% duty and 10% VAT apply to excess.
deMinimisNotes.BY: EAEU allowance: up to €200 (~$220) and 31 kg. 15% duty applies to excess + 10 Br fee.
deMinimisNotes.KG: EAEU allowance: up to €200 (~$220) and 31 kg. 15% duty applies to excess.
deMinimisNotes.TJ: Parcels up to $200 are duty-free. Standard national customs tariff applies to excess.
deMinimisNotes.IN: Gifts and personal imports up to ₹1,000 exempt; commercial parcels subject to BCD duty + 28% IGST.
deMinimisNotes.IT: EU regulations: VAT from €0, duty from €150 (~$165). Standard customs fee applies.
deMinimisNotes.GB: Goods valued up to £135 are exempt from customs duty (20% import VAT applies).

steps.title: Select regime, declarant and destination country
steps.desc: Choose your operation mode (import or export), declarant category (commercial company filing customs declaration or individual for personal use), and country of clearance (Uzbekistan, USA, Kazakhstan, UAE, Germany, Russia, Turkey, China).

steps.title: Classify by HS Code or enter from invoice
steps.desc: For Uzbekistan, an intelligent catalog of 10-digit national HS codes with indicative customs prices is available. For international shipments, easily enter the product name and 6-digit Harmonized System code directly from your contract.

steps.title: Determine CIF / CIP Customs Value (Incoterms 2020)
steps.desc: The taxable calculation base includes commercial invoice contract value plus international freight and transit insurance costs up to the port of entry border.

steps.title: Apply CT-1 preferences and duty-free allowances
steps.desc: Submitting an original Certificate of Origin (CT-1) for CIS goods exempts customs duties (0%). For individual postal parcels and baggage, De Minimis allowances are applied ($1,000/$2,000 in UZ, $800 in US, €200 in EAEU).

steps.title: Calculate duties, excise, VAT and export to PDF
steps.desc: The system computes an itemized breakdown of all levies in national currency and USD, ready to export into an official PDF report or share with your customs broker in one click.

factorsList.title: HS Code (Harmonized System)
factorsList.desc: Commodity nomenclature of foreign economic activity. The first 6 digits are uniform worldwide under World Customs Organization (WCO) standards. Each code determines base customs duty (0%–30%), excise tax, and non-tariff regulatory requirements (sanitary, phytosanitary, or certification compliance).

factorsList.title: Customs Duty Rate
factorsList.desc: Ad valorem duties are levied as a percentage of CIF customs value (e.g. 5%, 10%, 15%, 20%). Specific duties are charged per physical unit ($0.5/kg or /liter). Compound duties combine both methods (e.g., 15% but not less than $0.5/kg).

factorsList.title: VAT / Sales Tax in Destination Country
factorsList.desc: Levied at customs clearance. VAT is 12% in Uzbekistan and Kazakhstan, 20% in Russia, 19% in Germany, 20% in Turkey, 5% in UAE, while the US has 0% federal VAT. Applied on the taxable base: CIF Customs Value + Duty + Excise.

factorsList.title: Country of Origin & CT-1 Certificate
factorsList.desc: Importing goods originating from CIS Free Trade Agreement member states (Russia, Kazakhstan, Belarus, etc.) accompanied by an authentic CT-1 certificate grants a 0% duty rate. Developing nations can benefit from GSP/GSP+ tariff preferences.

factorsList.title: Customs Value (CIF / CIP Basis)
factorsList.desc: The statutory foundation for computing all import customs charges. Encompasses commercial invoice goods value PLUS documented international freight, loading, and transit insurance costs up to the customs border.

factorsList.title: Declarant Status (Individual vs Corporate)
factorsList.desc: Commercial entities declare goods via comprehensive customs declarations (CCD) paying full tariffs, excise, and VAT. Individuals importing for personal use benefit from preferential De Minimis limits, paying unified duties (30% in UZ, 15% in EAEU) only on excess value.

factorsList.title: Customs Indicative Risk Benchmark
factorsList.desc: Customs authorities maintain historical statistical value benchmarks per HS code. If declared invoice value is significantly below risk thresholds, customs officials may trigger valuation adjustments or request proof of international bank transfer.

factorsList.title: Excise Tax on Specific Goods
factorsList.desc: Applied to selected commodities: motor vehicles, industrial lubricants, gasoline, tobacco products, alcoholic beverages, and luxury perfumery. Calculated before VAT, expanding the taxable VAT base.

factorsList.title: Exchange Rate on Registration Date
factorsList.desc: All customs duties and taxes are officially settled in the national currency of the import jurisdiction (UZS, KZT, RUB, EUR, AED) at the Central Bank official exchange rate on the date of declaration submission.

faqList.question: How does the calculation work when another destination country is selected (USA, Kazakhstan, Russia, UAE, Germany, etc.)?
faqList.answer: The calculator features an intelligent adaptive engine. Selecting a destination country instantly shifts the tariff logic: applying the official currency (USD, KZT, RUB, EUR, TRY, AED, CNY), standard national duty rates, local VAT rates (12% in KZ, 20% in RU, 19% in DE, 0% in US), local processing fees (Merchandise Processing Fee in US, state customs fees in KZ and RU), and specific personal De Minimis rules (US Section 321 $800, EAEU €200).

faqList.question: Why does an HS code have 10 digits, and are codes identical across different countries?
faqList.answer: Classification follows the Harmonized System (HS) administered by the World Customs Organization (WCO). The first 6 digits are identical across more than 200 countries worldwide. Digits 7 and 8 define regional economic unions (CIS, EU CN, US HTSUS), while digits 9 and 10 provide national granularity. You can search by commodity name or 6-digit international code for any nation.

faqList.question: Can I input custom commodities manually or adjust duty and tax rates?
faqList.answer: Yes! Switch to 'Manual / Invoice' mode to enter any custom description, invoice article number, or national code. Additionally, dedicated quick-edit fields allow overriding import duty (%) and VAT (%) so you can model specific contractual or preferential terms.

faqList.question: Must freight delivery and insurance be included in customs value?
faqList.answer: Yes, mandatory. Under international customs valuation law and Incoterms (CIF / CIP border rules), customs taxable value includes invoice price PLUS international transport (freight), terminal handling, and cargo insurance until crossing the import border.

faqList.question: What is a CT-1 Certificate of Origin and how to receive a 0% duty rate?
faqList.answer: Form CT-1 certifies goods were manufactured or underwent sufficient transformation within CIS Free Trade Agreement countries (Uzbekistan, Russia, Kazakhstan, Belarus, etc.). Presenting a valid CT-1 grants a 0% import duty rate (VAT and clearance fees still apply).

faqList.question: What is the difference between commercial entity and individual calculation?
faqList.answer: Legal entities process commercial shipments with cargo declarations paying 100% of duties and taxes. Individuals importing for personal non-commercial use receive complete exemption (0%) up to established monetary and weight allowances. Exceeding allowances incurs unified duties (30% in UZ, 15% in EAEU) solely on the excess value.

faqList.question: What are customs indicative prices and why might the total change?
faqList.answer: Indicative prices are customs benchmarks used to prevent transfer-pricing undervaluation. If contract invoice prices are considerably below market profiles, customs inspectors may request bank payment receipts, export declarations from the origin country, or adjust the taxable customs value.

faqList.question: Can commercial entities reclaim or offset paid import VAT?
faqList.answer: Yes. If an enterprise is registered as a VAT taxpayer, import VAT paid upon customs declaration clearance with official bank payment confirmation is credited (offset) against output VAT in tax declarations.

faqList.question: What rules apply to international e-commerce packages (AliExpress, Amazon, eBay)?
faqList.answer: Special postal De Minimis limits apply: in Uzbekistan — up to $1,000 per calendar quarter (up to 30 kg); in EAEU (Kazakhstan, Russia) — up to €200 and 31 kg per parcel; in the US — up to $800 per day per recipient (Section 321). Values exceeding limits incur taxes on the differential.

faqList.question: How to save, print or send the calculation report?
faqList.answer: Click 'Download PDF' to produce a formal structured report complete with date stamps, commodity codes, and itemized calculations, or use 'Copy Calculation' to instantly send parameters via email or messenger.
